text.text_excerpt: Sarita's just keeps us coming back. We visit here frequently, for dine in and take out. My boyfriend loves the Cuban sandwiches, and I mean LOVES like there's nothing better than that sandwich. I usually get the quesadillas or the mexibowl, both are very tasty and made with fresh ingredients. The queso dip and chips they offer kind of taste like a cheap jar of queso dip you can get from the store, but hey, it's complimentary when you dine in, so no hard feelings there. Prices are fairly low, so you won't break the bank. The restaurant itself is very small, and their hours are weird. Those would be the only cons. Overall, we love this place and will keep coming back!

Sarita's is my favorite restaurant on Freret St. It's just around the corner from my house, so it's a natural choice for my family. We've eaten just about everything on the menu, and nothing disappoints. The fish taco is my favorite. The fish is fried crispy, and it's tucked into a flour tortilla with a helping of their house-made slaw. The cabbage and cilantro add crunch and flavor that takes it to the next level. After the fish taco comes the ropa viego plate. That whole platter is delicious. The sweet, slightly caramelized plantains, the savory shredded beef. Amazing. Love the cheese dip. We had a great meal at Sarita's over the weekend. The atmosphere was funky/cool but the music wasn't something we were crazy for. Management happily changed the music at our request and it made for a much more enjoyable experience. You must try the pork, really really good. Also the best plantains I have tasted in the city. This is my new favorite spot for Cuban fare and it is great to see a business making a go of it in the up-and-coming Freret neighborhood. My only suggestion would be the addition of Cuban coffee to the menu.
